The expressed αὐτοῦ carries the possessive, displacing the article's determiner (rule 20).
Imperative auxiliary rides with the verb, discontinuous under rule 15. Variant SBLGNT.ACT.1.20.v019 is underdetermined and its fallback carries the verb the English translates.

review_notes: *therein* is aligned rather than noncompositional: both source elements are visibly spelled in it (rules 35 and 81).
ὁ κατοικῶν splits with the article taking the single supplied nominal *man* and the participle its own verb (rules 32 and 90).

variant_decisions.evidence: Imperative λαβέτω against optative λάβοι. The ASV renders both third-person volitives with 'let' — compare 'Let his habitation be made desolate' for the imperative in the same verse — so 'His office let another take' does not distinguish the mood.

alignments.note: The ASV renders δεῖ in the following verse, writing *must* at ACT.1.22; this token's English stands there and nothing in this verse answers to it (rule 37). A reference comparison will report it as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.
Article takes *the* with the case preposition riding along, headed on *the* (rules 17 and 21).
The attributive participle is recast as a finite relative clause; the relativizer and auxiliary are its helpers (rules 7, 9 and 31).
The ASV writes an English verb word of its own for the compound, so the preposition realizing the dative's government rides with the governed pronoun (rules 21 and 106).
The ASV writes *all the time* as a bare adverbial with no preposition, so English realizes ἐν nowhere here (rule 36).
χρόνῳ is anarthrous, so the supplied determiner belongs to the noun (rules 51 and 58).
Variant SBLGNT.ACT.1.21.v020 is underdetermined and its fallback carries the relative the English translates.
*in* realizes the preverb εἰσ- inside the verb's own unit, headed on the verb word (rule 106).
*out* realizes the preverb ἐξ- inside the verb's own unit (rule 106).
Names split rather than sharing a head (rules 26 and 28).

review_notes: δεῖ is unrepresented under rule 37: its English *must* stands at ACT.1.22, which marks that word added with the matching note.
ἐν is unrepresented because the ASV writes the temporal phrase without a preposition (rule 36).

variant_decisions.evidence: The ASV's 'all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and went out' uses the bare English relative, which serves a temporal antecedent whether or not the Greek relative carries ἐν; it neither requires nor excludes the preposition.

alignments.note: The improper preposition is rendered by a single English word, so rule 71's frame question does not arise.
The genitive relative is rendered by the bare relativizer *that*.
*up* realizes the preverb ἀνα- inside the verb's own unit, headed on the verb word (rule 106).
Anarthrous noun with a supplied indefinite determiner as its helper (rule 51).
The expressed αὐτοῦ carries the possessive, displacing the article's determiner, and the ASV supplies it nothing else; the case preposition stays with the noun (rules 20 and 21).

Variant SBLGNT.ACT.1.22.v021 is underdetermined and its fallback carries the phrase the English translates.
The infinitive's English *become* stands with the supplied *must* of the preceding verse's δεῖ, which is its own added unit here.
Determinerless partitive genitive demonstrative: the case preposition rides with the demonstrative (rule 21).
*must* renders δεῖ, which stands at ACT.1.21 s001 and is left unrepresented there; this is a versification difference between the projection and the ASV, not a Greek idiom (rule 37).

review_notes: *must* is added with a note naming ACT.1.21, where δεῖ stands unrepresented; neither side reaches across (rule 37).
τῆς before ἀναστάσεως is emptied by the expressed αὐτοῦ under rule 20, so *of* stays with the noun.

variant_decisions.evidence: Word order only; 'must one become a witness with us' is the English order under either arrangement of σὺν ἡμῖν and γενέσθαι.

alignments.note: Supplied subject rides with the finite verb; *forward* completes the English verb's own expression as its helper (rules 7 and 9).
The ASV writes a bare participial *called* with no relativizer or determiner, so nothing answers to the article (rules 23 and 31).
The passive auxiliary rides with the verb (rule 9); head on the lexical verb.

review_notes: τόν before καλούμενον is unrepresented: the appositive is rendered by a bare participle with no relativizer for the article to keep (rule 31).

alignments.note: Supplied subject rides with the participle rendered as a finite verb (rules 7 and 9).
The juncture converting the participial clause into coordination is a helper on the finite verb it introduces (rules 29 and 88).
Anarthrous vocative with no supplied address word.

The compound noun καρδιογνώστης is recast as a finite relative clause; the relativizer and the object's determiner are its helpers (rules 7 and 31). Head on the word answering to the compound's core, the -γνώστης element, and not on the incorporated καρδιο- (rule 66's compound clause).
The substantival quantifier takes the case preposition and the supplied generic noun, headed on the quantifier (rules 17, 21 and 69).

review_notes: καρδιογνῶστα heads on *knowest*, the word answering to the compound's verbal core (rule 66); the supplied *who* and *the* ride inside its unit.
τῶν before δύο is emptied by the demonstrative τούτων under rule 38.

alignments.note: Infinitival marker is the verb's own helper, no conjunction governing the clause (rules 7 and 61).

variant_decisions.evidence: 'to take the place in this ministry' renders τόπον, and the same word recurs in 'go to his own place'; κλῆρον would be 'lot' or 'portion', which the ASV uses at 1:17 and 1:26 for that word.
